Geochelone nigra
Naive to the Gulapagos archi pelago, located west of continental Ecuador, the Galapagos Tortoise is the longest-lived vertebrate today. averaging more than 100 years (the oldest on record was over 150) This long-necked species is the largest extant tortoise, reaching weights of well over 400 pounds and a shell length of over 40 inches It can survive a year with no food or water

images.filename: Replica of King Cobra skull by Bone Clones.jpg
images.caption:
King Cobra
Ophiophagus hannah
Growing to a length of over 18 feet, the King Cobra is the largest venomous snake in the world. It can deliver enough venom in one bite to kill 20-30 people. Despite this, they are responsible for an average of only 5-10 deaths per year. King Cobras have excellent eyesight and appear to be very inquisitive and intelligent. Captives can reportedly recognize their keepers.
